Bee Swarm Collection / Removal

Please note - The Geelong Beekeepers Club is NOT a bee removal service. We MAY be able to assist depending on the circumstances, but as a group of volunteers, it's not possible for us to help in all instances.

Is it a swarm or an established/new hive?

Understanding the difference between a bee swarm and a hive or nest can determine the appropriate service you require for the bees to be removed safely.

Bee Swarms

Bee swarms are identified by a mass of bees clustered on a post or hanging from a tree or some other structure. The bees may stay in this cluster up to a few days while they look for a new home.

We recommend you contact one of the organisations or members listed on the club website as soon as possible, especially in relation to swarm bees, before they settle into a permanent place in your home - "Give them a call before they get into your wall".

Established Hives/Colonies

Bees moving in and out of a building wall, roof or chimney could indicate an established colony depending on how long they have been there.

If you can see honeycomb or the bees have been coming and going more than a week, chances are a hive is either well established or starting to establish.

For SWARM removal . .

Request assistance from a local beekeeper via the following sites.
LIST:Victorian Apiarists' Association Swarm Catcher Locator
LIST:International Swarm Patrol website - complete the online form. They have a number of beekeepers registered with the site who can contact you to arrange for removal. https://www.swarmpatrol.com/swarm_reports/add
LIST:Aussie Apiarists Online - https://aussieapiaristsonline.net/bee-removal.html
LIST:Bee Rescue: Geelong, Bellarine, Surfcoast & District Facebook group - https://www.facebook.com/groups/809538203147190

The Geelong Beekeepers Club is a volunteer organisation and has limited resources to assist with the removal of swarms and in particular established colonies. To assist the public with the safe removal or relocation of bee swarms and colonies, the above resources have been provided.

For Hive removal . .

To remove an established colony from inside a building (called a "Cut out") requires specialist skills and equipment as well as appropriate insurance. A suitably qualified Bee Removal Specialist will most likely charge a fee to remove the hive in this case.

Bee colonies can also exist out in the open where you will also see the honeycomb.

What can you do if you suspect an established hive in a building structure?
LIST:Request help from a local beekeeper from the options listed previously.
LIST:Engage a Bee Removal Specialist such as Bee Removals Victoria - https://beeremovals.com.au/

Club members who collect swarms

A list of Geelong Beekeepers Club members who may be able to collect free-hanging and accessible swarms in the Geelong district, with their areas and costs, is kept on the club website's Swarm Removal page. Most do not do "cut outs".

For a beekeeper to determine their ability and capacity to assist you, it is helpful to provide the following information:
LIST:Location (including suburb and where the hive is living such as inside a wall, chimney, roof or type of container such as compost bin)
LIST:Provide a photo if safe to do so
LIST:State how long the bees have been there
LIST:Contact details such as phone or email

Depending on the difficulty or distance travelled to remove the bees, it is not unreasonable for the beekeeper to charge for their services. If it is an easy swarm removal, most beekeepers will provide a free service. We recommend asking the beekeeper if a fee will be charged before accepting their assistance.
